chunk_findings.detail: `command_provenance` decides whether the last writer of `[gate.<id>].command` was the committed or the local layer by *position* in the list: `is_local = n >= len(paths) // 2`. That is only correct when `tomlcfg.config_paths(root, "gates.toml")` returns exactly two equal, fixed halves laid out committed-then-local. It breaks for any other shape, and the required evidence schema shows a third layer exists: the failing-first test must record `command_layer` ∈ `'committed' | 'local' | 'env'`, yet this function can only ever return `'committed'` or `'local'` (`layer` is assigned only those two literals, default `"committed"`). So an env-layer command is always mislabelled. Concretely, with the list `[.ddflow/config.toml, .ddflow/gates.toml, <env-provided gates file>, .ddflow/local/config.toml, .ddflow/local/gates.toml]` (`len == 5`, `len//2 == 2`), the env path at index 2 satisfies `n >= 2`, so a pass whose command came from the environment layer records `command_layer: "local"` instead of `"env"` and the renderer prints "passed with a local-only command (not the committed one)" for a pass that is not a local-layer pass at all — the exact class of provenance mislabelling B924bdc92d7 is about, just with `env` instead of `local`. The same positional assumption also misfires on any odd-length list: if `config_paths` omits non-existent files (the `if not Path(path).is_file(): continue` guard in this very function implies paths may be filtered/absent), a repo with only the committed `.ddflow/config.toml` present yields `len(paths) == 1`, `len//2 == 0`, so index 0 gets `is_local = True` and a plain committed-command pass is reported as a local-only pass (and `committed_command` stays `""`), failing the "nothing extra for a committed-command pass" requirement. The layer should be taken from the layer identity recorded while overlaying (as the intent states), not inferred from the index. Note the README hunk itself documents only `"local"` (else `"committed"`), consistent with

chunk_findings.detail: The "differs" clause is decided by the *presence* of `ev["committed_command_digest"]`, never by comparing it against the pass's own `command_digest`, even though the function's docstring promises it fires only "when the evidence shows the committed layer defined a **different** one". Concretely: committed config sets `[gate.unit_tests].command = "pytest -q"`, and a user's `.ddflow/local/config.toml` sets the identical string `"pytest -q"` (a common thing to do when copying the committed command into a local file that also adjusts thresholds). The overlay in `defs.py` then marks `command_layer = "local"` (the local layer is the last to set it), the runner records `command_digest` for `"pytest -q"` and `committed_command_digest` for the identical committed string, and this function appends `"; the committed command differs"` to a pass whose command is byte-for-byte the committed command — a false provenance claim of exactly the kind B924bdc92d7 is meant to eliminate. Conversely, if the runner records only the additive keys named in the change description (`command_layer`, `command_digest`, `output_log_host`) and no `committed_command_digest`, the clause is dead code and regression-test assertion (3) ("the label says the committed command differs") can never pass. Either way the function needs to compare `ev.get("command_digest") != ev.get("committed_command_digest")` (or whatever key the runner actually writes) rather than testing key existence.
